*UW–Madison · PSYC 752 Machine Learning*

Adapted from John Curtin’s Unit 4 classification lab and starter Quarto template. I developed the feature recipes, compared four configurations on the course validation split, and submitted predictions from the sex-by-passenger-class model. That submission placed first in the class’s held-out prediction challenge.

## Data and evaluation

The outcome is passenger survival. I fit the preprocessing recipes and models on the training split and measured classification accuracy on the validation split. All four configurations use quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA), fitted through the regularized discriminant analysis interface with both covariance regularization parameters set to zero.

To render this report, install the R packages tidymodels, discrim, and klaR and put the cleaned course CSVs in a local `data/` directory next to this file. The training and validation files are required. The course test file is only needed to generate predictions. Run `quarto render fit_rda.qmd` from the repository root.

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidymodels)
library(discrim)

data_dir <- "data"

read_split <- function(filename) {
  read_csv(file.path(data_dir, filename), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
}

data_trn <- read_split("titanic_train_cln.csv") |>
  mutate(survived = as.factor(survived))
data_val <- read_split("titanic_val_cln.csv") |>
  mutate(survived = as.factor(survived))

qda_spec <- discrim_regularized(frac_common_cov = 0, frac_identity = 0) |>
  set_engine("klaR")
```

## Feature engineering

### Baseline with family size

I combined the counts of accompanying relatives into a single family-size feature and log-transformed fare.

```{r}
#| label: recipe-1

rec_rda_1 <- recipe(
  survived ~ age + fare + sex + n_sib_spouse + n_parent_child,
  data = data_trn) |>
  step_impute_median(age) |>
  step_mutate(
    fare_log = log1p(fare),
    family_size = n_sib_spouse + n_parent_child + 1,
    female = if_else(sex == "female", 1, 0)) |>
  step_rm(fare, sex, n_sib_spouse, n_parent_child) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
```

### Fare per family member and log age

I added passenger class and divided fare by recorded family size to explore a fare measure adjusted for group size. I used a log transform for age.

```{r}
#| label: recipe-2

rec_rda_2 <- recipe(
  survived ~ age + fare + sex + n_sib_spouse + n_parent_child + pclass,
  data = data_trn) |>
  step_impute_median(age) |>
  step_mutate(
    family_size = n_sib_spouse + n_parent_child + 1,
    fare_per_person = fare / family_size,
    female = if_else(sex == "female", 1, 0),
    age_child = log1p(age)) |>
  step_rm(fare, sex, n_sib_spouse, n_parent_child, age) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
```

### Sex by passenger class

I wanted to give the classifier a feature that could capture differences in survival patterns by sex across passenger classes. I multiplied a female indicator by the numeric passenger-class code and also included an indicator for traveling alone and one for embarking at Southampton.

```{r}
#| label: recipe-3

rec_rda_3 <- recipe(
  survived ~ age + fare + sex + pclass + n_sib_spouse + n_parent_child + embarked,
  data = data_trn) |>
  step_impute_median(age) |>
  step_impute_mode(embarked) |>
  step_mutate(
    female = if_else(sex == "female", 1, 0),
    fare_log = log1p(fare),
    family_size = n_sib_spouse + n_parent_child + 1,
    is_alone = if_else(family_size == 1, 1, 0),
    embarked_S = if_else(embarked == "S", 1, 0),
    female_x_pclass = female * pclass) |>
  step_rm(fare, sex, embarked, n_sib_spouse, n_parent_child) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
```

### Child indicator

I tested whether an indicator for passengers under 14 added information alongside continuous age. This exploratory recipe centers age within each split when the features are generated.

```{r}
#| label: recipe-4

rec_rda_4 <- recipe(
  survived ~ age + fare + sex + pclass + n_sib_spouse + n_parent_child,
  data = data_trn) |>
  step_impute_median(age) |>
  step_mutate(
    female = if_else(sex == "female", 1, 0),
    fare_log = log1p(fare),
    family_size = n_sib_spouse + n_parent_child + 1,
    is_child = if_else(age < 14, 1, 0),
    age_centered = age - mean(age)) |>
  step_rm(sex, fare, n_sib_spouse, n_parent_child, age) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
```

## Validation results

The original course run produced the following validation results. Each configuration changes several predictors, so the table compares complete recipes.

| Configuration | Validation accuracy |
| --- | ---: |
| Baseline with family size | 79.7% |
| Fare per family member and log age | 80.5% |
| Sex by passenger class | **81.3%** |
| Child indicator | 80.9% |

The code below recomputes the comparison from the local course splits.

```{r}
#| label: validation

fit_and_validate <- function(feature_recipe) {
  prepared_recipe <- prep(feature_recipe, training = data_trn)
  train_features <- bake(prepared_recipe, new_data = NULL)
  validation_features <- bake(prepared_recipe, new_data = data_val)

  model <- fit(qda_spec, survived ~ ., data = train_features)
  predictions <- predict(model, validation_features, type = "class")

  list(
    recipe = prepared_recipe,
    model = model,
    accuracy = accuracy_vec(validation_features$survived, predictions$.pred_class)
  )
}

results <- list(
  "Baseline with family size" = fit_and_validate(rec_rda_1),
  "Fare per family member and log age" = fit_and_validate(rec_rda_2),
  "Sex by passenger class" = fit_and_validate(rec_rda_3),
  "Child indicator" = fit_and_validate(rec_rda_4)
)

validation_results <- tibble(
  configuration = names(results),
  validation_accuracy = vapply(results, function(result) result$accuracy, numeric(1))
)

knitr::kable(validation_results, digits = 3)
```

## Held-out predictions

I submitted the sex-by-passenger-class model, which had the highest validation accuracy among the four QDA recipes. The code applies the same training-fitted recipe to the course test split and writes the predicted survival class for each passenger. The test split’s labels were withheld by the course.

```{r}
#| label: test-predictions

test_file <- "titanic_test_cln.csv"
unlabeled_test_file <- "titanic_test_cln_no_label.csv"

if (file.exists(file.path(data_dir, unlabeled_test_file))) {
  test_file <- unlabeled_test_file
}

if (file.exists(file.path(data_dir, test_file))) {
  submitted <- results[["Sex by passenger class"]]
  test_data <- read_split(test_file) |> select(-any_of("survived"))
  test_features <- bake(submitted$recipe, new_data = test_data)

  test_predictions <- tibble(
    passenger_id = test_data$passenger_id,
    survived = predict(submitted$model, test_features, type = "class")$.pred_class
  )

  write_csv(test_predictions, file.path(data_dir, "test_preds_dang.csv"))
} else {
  cat("The course test CSV is optional. No predictions were exported.")
}
```
